claims.statement: package.json/README describe commander as 'the complete solution for node.js command-line programs'
Commander is strict: errors on unrecognised options, missing/excess arguments, missing mandatory options
Zero production dependencies is a stated, enforced design principle
Commander 14 requires Node.js >= 20
Release policy: major releases ~every 6 months, node minimum bumped at LTS EOL, old majors get security updates for 12 months
CI runs jest + check (type/lint/format) on node 20/22/24 across ubuntu/windows/macos
Help option -h,--help is lazy-created per command; implicit help command auto-added when subcommands exist and no action handler
Option values stored separately from command properties since v7; storeOptionsAsProperties() is the legacy escape hatch
TypeScript typings are hand-maintained (typings/index.d.ts, 1113 lines) and checked via tsd + tsc on JS (JSDoc) and TS
Action handler receives declared argument values, then options object (or command in legacy mode), then command; async handlers require parseAsync
Option parsing dispatches values via EventEmitter events ('option:name', 'optionEnv:name') that are also a documented public API
Multiple parse() calls supported since 13.0 via saveStateBeforeParse/restoreStateBeforeParse; throws for storeOptionsAsProperties
Executable subcommands spawn child processes, forward signals, increment inspector port
Security reports handled via Tidelift, not public issues
Deprecated-but-supported features are tracked in docs/deprecated.md (9+ items, some dating from v3/v7/v8)
Recent git history (2024-10 .. 2026-02) is dominated by dependabot dependency bumps; human commits are John Gee (shadowspawn) and abetomo plus occasional contributors
Test suite: 109 jest test files, coverage collection enabled but no coverageThreshold in jest.config.js
Funding/backing: GitHub sponsors for abetomo and shadowspawn; Tidelift subscription for commercial support
Parsing handles negative numbers as option-arguments when unambiguous, Electron detection, node --eval detection, '--' literal handling
Each _executeSubCommand call registers 5 persistent process signal listeners (SIGUSR1/2, SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) that are never removed
Help output is generated by the Help class (747 lines) with style/format hooks, grouping (v14), wrapping, color support
Jest coverage is collected but no coverageThreshold is configured (no enforcement gate)
The internal parse dispatch uses negative-number heuristics and an activeGroup/activeVariadicOption state machine in parseOptions (command.js:1748-1895)
README documents features comprehensively (options, commands, help, hooks, parsing config, TS, support) with examples and a zh-CN translation
Typing drift: typings/index.d.ts declares CommanderError.nestedError as string, but runtime assigns an Error (command.js wraps spawn errors in it) and the test suite reads nestedError.code
_executeSubCommand registers 5 process signal listeners per invocation, never removed; accumulates only in long-lived parents (exitOverride path)
jest collectCoverage true but no coverageThreshold; coverage can regress without CI failing

Version trajectory (from changelog): 3.0.0 2019-08, 7.0.0 2021-01, 9.0.0 2022-01, 10.0.0 2023-01, 11.0.0 2023-06, 12.0.0 2024-02, 13.0.0 2024-12, 14.0.0 2025-05 — ~2 majors/year recently, consistent with 'major ~every 6 months' policy
No CVEs/GHSAs found against the commander package itself; the only related 2025 advisory is MAL-2025-192687 for the typosquat package 'commander-stable'
Funding: GitHub sponsors shadowspawn (John Gee), abetomo, tj; Tidelift subscription channel
Upstream has released v15.0.0 (post-snapshot); the snapshot at v14.0.3 (2026-02-02) is one major version behind current upstream
No security advisories against the commander package itself; known advisories target typosquats ('commander-js' GHSA-2hqf-qqmq-pgpp; 'commander-stable' MAL-2025-192687)
Node 20 LTS reaches end-of-life 2026-04-30; per commander's stated policy the next major (v15) bumps the minimum Node version (snapshot requires >=20)
commander is in the >10M weekly downloads category (exact figure not retrievable in this session; web_fetch unavailable)

Ecosystem: major orgs (GitLab, Keycloak, bitwarden, zendesk) use commander; competitor releases observed (yargs 18.x, meow ~14.x, clipanion 4.0-rc); some migration chatter toward commander, no evidence of mass migration away

hypotheses.statement: commander.js is a mature (~13-year) single-purpose CLI-parsing library in steady maintenance mode: slow feature growth, aggressive backward compatibility, zero runtime dependencies, hand-maintained typings, comprehensive tests; primary risks are bus factor, parse-edge-case complexity, and legacy compatibility burden rather than feature gaps.

Revised: commander.js is a mature, healthy, deliberately conservative library; the analyzed snapshot (v14.0.3, 2026-02-02) is one major version behind upstream (v15.0.0 released 2026), so any change proposed against this snapshot must first be reconciled with the v15 delta rather than built blind.
